'''Monica Vișan''' (born August 5, 1979, in [[Drobeta-Turnu Severin]], [[Romania]]) is a Romanian mathematician at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] who specializes in [[Partial differential equation|partial differential equations]] and is well known for her work on the [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation]].

==Education and career==
Vișan earned a bachelor's degree at the [[University of Bucharest]] in 2002.{{r|cv}}
She became a student of [[Terence Tao]] at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), where she completed her doctorate in 2006. Her dissertation was titled ''The Defocusing Energy-Critical Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation in Dimensions Five and Higher''.{{r|cv|mgp}}

After postdoctoral research at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], Vișan became an assistant professor in the mathematics department at the [[University of Chicago]] in 2008. She returned to UCLA as a faculty member in 2009 and (keeping her appointment at UCLA) spent 2010–2011 as Harrington Faculty Fellow at the [[University of Texas at Austin]].{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Vișan won a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 2010.{{r|sloan}} She was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the 2024 class of fellows.{{r|fams}}

==Selected publications==
With [[Herbert Koch]] and [[Daniel Tătaru]], Vișan is the author of the book ''Dispersive Equations and Nonlinear Waves: Generalized Korteweg–de Vries, Nonlinear Schrödinger, Wave and Schrödinger Maps''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Koch |first1=Herbert |last2=Tataru |first2=Daniel |last3=Vis̜an |first3=Monica |title=Dispersive Equations and Nonlinear Waves: Generalized Korteweg–de Vries, Nonlinear Schrödinger, Wave and Schrödinger Maps |date=2014 |publisher=Birkhäuser |location=Basel |isbn=978-3-0348-0735-7 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265574274 |access-date=4 November 2025 |language=en}} {{doi|10.1007/978-3-0348-0736-4|doi-access=free}}</ref>
